identificationModule.briefTitle: Intralesional Bevacizumab Injection on Primary Pterygium
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Intralesional Bevacizumab Injection on Primary Pterygium: Preliminary Results

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate that intralesional injection of bevacizumab on primary pterygium can reduce the corneal pterygium area, inflammation, redness and other symptoms.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intralesional injection of bevacizumab on primary pterygium treatment

armGroups.label: Topical antihistamine and vasoconstrictor
armGroups.description: combination of topical antazoline HCl 0.05% and tetrahydrozoline HCl 0.04%

interventions.name: Intralesional injection of bevacizumab
interventions.description: single dose of 2 mg of bevacizumab intralesional injection on pterygium Combination of topical antazoline and tetrahydrozoline four times a day

primaryOutcomes.description:
Prior to receive the treatments, patients were asked to evaluate grading of their own symptoms and underwent clinical grading of the elevation and inflammation of the lesions using slit lamp biomicroscopy by an opthalmologist (OE). Digital photographs of each eye with pterygium were obtained for corneal pterygium area analysis \[Sony Mavica digital still camera MVC-FD83, Japan\]. Each patient was randomly assigned into either treatment group or control group using computer-generated random numbers table.

Number of patients with adverse events will be recorded.
